strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across 5 diverse spatiotemporal domains (fluid dynamics, neural calcium imaging, facial expressions, neurostimulation, monkey reaching) with consistent improvements over baselines
Elegant dual-space architecture cleanly separates trajectory editing (low-dimensional C) from high-fidelity rendering (high-dimensional Z), avoiding optimization conflicts
Solid empirical results: 35.7 PSNR vs 28.3 for linear baselines in fluid dynamics; E-field classification F1 improves from 0.30 to 0.63 in contrastive space
Multiple editing operators (splines, Taylor extrapolation, KDE-based class traversal) demonstrate flexibility of learned manifold for different control tasks
Excellent reproducibility: comprehensive appendices with full hyperparameters, algorithms, runtimes (Tables 4-5), model sizes, and promised code release; public dataset with full simulation protocols

Disentanglement evidence: orthogonality analysis (Table 6) shows contrastive space better separates temporal variations (0.0155 cosine similarity) from confounding factors vs raw diffusion latents (0.1014)
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging trade-offs: lossiness of embedding, local-only traversals, DDIM inversion requirements, without overselling
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (contrastive learning from Chen et al. 2020, diffusion from Rombach et al. 2022, trajectory modeling via splines/finite differences) without fundamental algorithmic innovation or theoretical contribution

Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing recent diffusion editing methods (DiffEdit, Masactually, SEGA), lacks quantitative comparisons to ControlNet and InstructPix2Pix despite mentioning them as limitations, no comparison to Neural ODEs directly on latent space

Insufficient theoretical justification: Why does contrastive learning specifically help trajectory modeling? No formal analysis of when/why dual-space helps. Could improvements simply reflect easier spline fitting in lower dimensions rather than better dynamics alignment?

Design choices lack justification: contrastive similarity uses unusual L2 distance rather than standard dot product/cosine; uniform kNN weights despite distance-based weighting seeming more principled; embedding dimension selection (d=8 vs d=3) appears arbitrary without principled criteria

Computational efficiency concerns: requires training VAE (83.65M params) + cLDM (113.68M) + CEBRA encoder; evaluation ~5 min/batch due to 1000-step DDIM inversion; scalability to higher resolutions (1024×1024) unclear; all experiments use 256×256 images

Method requires domain-specific auxiliary labels (time, action units, coil angles) with no guidance on selection for new domains; no zero-shot/few-shot capabilities; full retraining needed for new datasets, limiting practical applicability

Experimental limitations: calcium imaging converted to RGB (potential information loss, why not work directly on time-series?); DISFA limited to 12 action units; TMS dataset severely imbalanced (30 responders vs 80 non-responders); monkey reaching only compared to PCA, not other structured latent methods; no human perceptual studies

Technical issues: finite-difference derivatives in Taylor extrapolation (Eq. 7) noise robustness not analyzed; KDE-based class traversal appears ad-hoc mixing supervised contrastive learning with unsupervised KDE; DDIM inversion quality not quantified, failure modes not discussed

Analysis gaps: near-zero RMSE in C-space (Table 1) raises questions about numerical precision/overfitting; KDE interpolation only shown for binary classification without multi-class generalization analysis; orthogonality analysis limited to single confounding factor (Reynolds number); no failure case analysis or guidance on method limitations

Missing theoretical understanding: why does dimensional reduction specifically structure dynamics? Why contrastive learning over alternatives (VAE disentanglement, other manifold learning)? Relationships between three editing operators not well explained

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across five diverse spatiotemporal domains (fluid dynamics, neural imaging, facial expressions, neurostimulation, monkey motor control) with consistent improvements (e.g., 35.7 vs 28.3 PSNR in fluid dynamics)
Practical plug-and-play architecture that is solver-agnostic (works with DDIM, Rex-RK4, IsoDiff) and requires no modifications to pretrained diffusion models
Solid experimental methodology with multiple metrics, thoughtful ablations (kNN vs MLP, embedding dimensions, solver comparisons), and proper generalization testing on held-out segments
Clear and honest presentation with well-motivated problem, good visualizations, and transparent limitations discussion
Strong reproducibility with explicit algorithms, detailed hyperparameters, documented computational costs, and code release promised
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for why supervised InfoNCE loss specifically yields dynamics-aware geometry; core claim that grouping same-label samples creates dynamics structure lacks principled explanation, given that different trajectories at identical timesteps can have divergent dynamics

Fundamental many-to-one lossy embedding limitation inadequately addressed; kNN lifting is a workaround rather than solution, and end-to-end decoder training (mentioned as future work) is central to reliability but not pursued

Insufficient design justifications: (1) Why L2 distance instead of standard cosine similarity in InfoNCE? No ablation provided. (2) Positive window Δ definition is domain-specific with no principled setting approach. (3) Why nonlinear operators (splines, TEX) work in C-space but not Z-space is empirically shown but conceptually unexplained

Limited methodological novelty: combines existing techniques (diffusion inversion, supervised InfoNCE, kNN decoding, standard trajectory models); main contribution is architectural integration rather than fundamental advance

Incomplete experimental comparisons: (1) ControlNet/InstructPix2Pix mentioned as limitations but never rigorously compared despite addressing similar control goals. (2) Physics-informed priors (Shu et al. 2023) discussed but not empirically compared. (3) IsoDiff comparison (Table 10) applies ConDA on top of IsoDiff rather than direct comparison. (4) CcGAN baseline relegated to appendix

Conceptual gap: standard contrastive learning clusters augmentations of same sample, but here samples with identical auxiliary labels but different dynamics are grouped; why this creates dynamics-aware rather than just auxiliary-variable-aware geometry is unclear
Missing ablations on contrastive design (temperature τ sensitivity, L2 vs cosine distance) and limited analysis of what C-space dimensions actually encode (dynamics vs auxiliary variables)

Modest improvements for some tasks: n-step prediction (Table 2) shows near-zero RMSE for multiple methods, and E-field classification (F1=0.63) remains low in absolute terms despite improvements over Z-space
